# AI Report Generator
[Repo Link](https://rocscience.visualstudio.com/Hackathons/_git/ArmenCristianReportGenerator)

A Streamlit-based web application that generates professional PDF and markdown reports from multiple file types (PDF, DOCX, markdown, text, images) using customizable templates and optional LLM-powered content enhancement.

## Overview

This project provides an intuitive web interface for combining content from various document formats into unified, professionally formatted reports. Users can upload multiple files, select from pre-built templates (academic, business, technical), customize the output, and generate polished PDF or markdown documents.

## Key Features

- **Multi-format Support**: Process PDF, DOCX, markdown, text files, and images
- **Template System**: Choose from academic, business, or technical report templates
- **LLM Enhancement**: Optional OpenAI integration for content improvement and formatting
- **Live Preview**: See your report before generating
- **Export Options**: Download as PDF or markdown

## Quick Start

### Prerequisites
- Python 3.8 or higher
- OpenAI API key (optional, for LLM features)

### Installation

1. Navigate to the application directory:
   ```bash
   cd ai-report-generator
   ```

2. Create and activate a virtual environment:
   ```bash
   # Windows
   python -m venv venv
   venv\Scripts\activate
   
   # Linux/Mac
   python -m venv venv
   source venv/bin/activate
   ```

3. Install dependencies:
   ```bash
   pip install -r requirements.txt
   ```

4. (Optional) Set up environment variables:
   ```bash
   # Copy the example file
   copy .env.example .env  # Windows
   # or
   cp .env.example .env    # Linux/Mac
   
   # Edit .env and add your OPENAI_API_KEY
   ```

5. Run the application:
   ```bash
   python -m streamlit run app.py
   ```

The application will open at `http://localhost:8501`

For detailed setup instructions, see [GETTING_STARTED.md](GETTING_STARTED.md).

## Project Structure

```
ArmenCristianReportGenerator/
├── ai-report-generator/          # Main application directory
│   ├── app.py                    # Streamlit application entry point
│   ├── pages/                    # Multi-page Streamlit interface
│   ├── components/               # Reusable UI components
│   ├── utils/                    # Core processing modules
│   ├── templates/                # Report templates
│   └── requirements.txt          # Python dependencies
├── GETTING_STARTED.md            # Detailed setup guide
└── README.md                     # This file
```

## Technology Stack

- **Frontend**: Streamlit
- **Backend**: Python 3.8+
- **PDF Generation**: WeasyPrint / ReportLab
- **LLM Integration**: OpenAI API
- **File Processing**: pypdf, python-docx, Pillow, langchain

## Documentation

- **[GETTING_STARTED.md](GETTING_STARTED.md)** - Complete setup and installation guide
- **[ai-report-generator/README.md](ai-report-generator/README.md)** - Application-specific documentation
- **[ai-report-generator/docs/](ai-report-generator/docs/)** - Architecture, components, and development roadmap

## Usage

1. **Upload Files**: Select multiple files from your computer
2. **Choose Template**: Pick a template style or provide custom instructions
3. **Configure**: Set title, author, date, and optional logo
4. **Preview**: Review the generated content
5. **Generate**: Download your report as PDF or markdown

## Development

This is a hackathon project. For development guidelines and roadmap, see the [documentation](ai-report-generator/docs/) in the application directory.

## License

Hackathon project - internal use only.

# 🏗️ AI-Powered Geotechnical Report Generator

An intelligent, locally-hosted Streamlit application that generates professional geotechnical engineering reports using AI. Upload your investigation data, select a template, and let AI create comprehensive, well-structured reports in multiple formats.

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-3.8%2B-blue)
![Streamlit](https://img.shields.io/badge/Streamlit-1.28%2B-red)
![OpenAI](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenAI-GPT--4-green)
![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Internal%20Use-orange)

---

## 📋 Table of Contents

- [Features](#-features)
- [Quick Start](#-quick-start)
- [Installation](#-installation)
- [Configuration](#-configuration)
- [Usage Guide](#-usage-guide)
- [Supported Formats](#-supported-formats)
- [Architecture](#-architecture)
- [Troubleshooting](#-troubleshooting)
- [Best Practices](#-best-practices)
- [Project Structure](#-project-structure)

---

## ✨ Features

### 🤖 **AI-Powered Generation**
- Utilizes OpenAI's GPT-4 models to analyze geotechnical data
- Intelligent document classification and content extraction
- Context-aware section generation following engineering standards

### 📁 **Multi-Format Input**
- **Documents**: PDF, DOCX, TXT, Markdown
- **Data Files**: CSV, XLSX
- **Images**: PNG, JPG, JPEG

### 📄 **Template System**
- Upload your own report templates (Markdown or PDF)
- AI extracts structure and style from existing reports
- Use default professional geotechnical template
- Section-based instructions for consistent formatting

### ⬇️ **Multiple Export Formats**
- **Markdown** (.md) - Clean, portable text format
- **HTML** (.html) - Web-ready with professional styling
- **PDF** (.pdf) - Print-ready professional documents
- **Word** (.docx) - Editable Microsoft Word format
---

## 🚀 Quick Start

### Prerequisites

- **Python 3.8 or higher** - [Download here](https://www.python.org/downloads/)
- **OpenAI API Key** - [Get one here](https://platform.openai.com/api-keys)
- **Internet Connection** - Required for AI processing

### Installation

1. **Clone or download this repository**

2. **Navigate to the project directory**

   cd path\to\Agentic-Report-generator-EW-BY
2. **Create and activate a virtual environment**

   python -m venv venv
   venv\Scripts\activate
2. **Install dependencies:**

   pip install -r requirements.txt
   3. **Set up your OpenAI API key:**
   
   Create a `.env` file in the project root:
   OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-your-actual-api-key-here
   4. **Launch the application:**
   
   **Windows:**
   run_dashboard.bat
      **Mac/Linux:**
   ./run_dashboard.sh
      **Or directly:**
   streamlit run app.py
   5. **Access the dashboard:**
   - Opens automatically in your browser
   - Or navigate to: `http://localhost:8501`

---

## 🔧 Configuration

### Required Setup

#### 1. OpenAI API Key

The application requires an OpenAI API key to function. Get one from [OpenAI Platform](https://platform.openai.com/api-keys).

**Option 1: Using .env file (Recommended)**
# Create .env file in project root
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-your-key-here**Option 2: Environment Variable**
# Windows (PowerShell)
$env:OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-your-key-here"

# Mac/Linux
export OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-your-key-here"### Optional Configuration

- **AI Model Selection**: Choose between GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4-turbo, GPT-3.5-turbo
- **Report Metadata**: Project name, author, date
- **Include/Exclude**: Images, metadata sections

---

## 📖 Usage Guide

### Step 1: Input Tab - Upload Files

1. Navigate to the **📁 Input** tab
2. **Upload Data Files:**
   - Click "Upload your files"
   - Select PDFs, Word docs, text files, spreadsheets, or images
   - Multiple files supported
   
3. **Upload Template:**
   - Upload a Markdown template, OR
   - Upload a PDF report (AI will extract the structure)

4. **Configure Report:**
   - Select output format (Markdown, PDF, HTML, DOCX)
   - Enter report title
   - Add project name
   - Add author name
   - Set report date

5. **Generate:**
   - Click **🚀 Generate Report**
   - Wait for processing (typically 30-90 seconds)

### Step 2: Template Tab - Review Structure

- View template sections automatically detected
- See the template preview
- Verify section headings match your needs

### Step 3: Report Tab - View & Download

1. **Select Sections:**
   - Choose which sections to include
   
2. **Preview:**
   - View the generated report content
   - Check formatting and content quality
   
3. **Download:**
   - Select desired format from dropdown
   - Click **📥 Download** button
   - File saves with timestamp

---

## 📦 Supported Formats

### Input Formats

| Type | Extensions | Notes |
|------|------------|-------|
| **Documents** | `.pdf`, `.docx`, `.txt`, `.md` | Text extraction with classification |

# AI Report Generator

A WPF desktop application that leverages OpenAI's GPT-4 to generate professional engineering technical reports from source documents. Built with .NET 8 and designed for structural engineering teams at Rocscience.

![.NET 8](https://img.shields.io/badge/.NET-8.0-512BD4)
![WPF](https://img.shields.io/badge/WPF-Windows-0078D7)
![OpenAI](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenAI-GPT--4o-412991)

## Features

- **AI-Powered Report Generation**: Uses OpenAI GPT-4o to intelligently synthesize content from multiple source documents into a cohesive technical report
- **Multi-Format Input Support**: Import PDFs, text files, markdown documents, and images as source material
- **Template-Based Structure**: Define your report structure using customizable markdown templates
- **Real-Time Streaming**: Watch your report generate in real-time with streaming AI output
- **Live Markdown Preview**: Toggle between edit mode and rendered preview using WebView2
- **PDF Export**: Export your reports to PDF with automatic table of contents generation
- **Appendix Management**: Attach PDF appendices that are automatically merged with cover pages during export
- **Smart Content Handling**: Option to preserve original content ("Keep as-is") for text/markdown files
- **Company Branding**: Add your company logo and information that persists between sessions
- **Image Insertion**: Insert images from your source files directly into the report with markdown syntax

## Requirements

- Windows 10/11
- .NET 8.0 SDK
- WebView2 Runtime (usually pre-installed on Windows 10/11)

## Getting Started

### Running from Cursor IDE

The easiest way to launch the application is directly from Cursor:

1. Open the project folder in Cursor
2. Open the integrated terminal (`Ctrl+``)
3. Navigate to the project directory and run:

```powershell
cd ReportGenerator
dotnet run
```

Alternatively, you can use Cursor's built-in run functionality or ask the AI assistant to launch the program for you.

### Running from Command Line

```powershell
cd ReportGenerator
dotnet build
dotnet run
```

### Building for Release

```powershell
cd ReportGenerator
dotnet publish -c Release
```

The executable will be located in `bin/Release/net8.0-windows/publish/`.

## Usage

### 1. Add Source Files
Click **"+ Add Files"** to import your source documents:
- **PDF files** - Extracted text and tables are parsed automatically
- **Text/Markdown files** - Can optionally be preserved as-is without AI modification
- **Images** - Referenced in the report using markdown image syntax

### 2. Configure Report Settings
- Select or import a **report template** to define the structure
- Fill in **company information** (saved automatically for future sessions)
- Add a **company logo** for the cover page
- Optionally add **appendix PDFs** to attach at the end

### 3. Generate Report
Click **"🤖 Generate Report"** to start AI generation. The report streams in real-time - watch as each section is created based on your source materials.

### 4. Edit & Preview
- Toggle between **Edit Mode** (raw markdown) and **Preview Mode** (rendered HTML)
- Insert images using the toolbar buttons
- Make manual adjustments as needed

### 5. Export
Click **"💾 Export PDF"** to save your report:
- **PDF format** - Rendered with proper styling, optional table of contents, and merged appendices
- **Markdown format** - Raw markdown with appendix content extracted

## Dependencies

- [CommunityToolkit.Mvvm](https://www.nuget.org/packages/CommunityToolkit.Mvvm) - MVVM framework
- [Microsoft.Web.WebView2](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Web.WebView2) - Markdown preview rendering
- [OpenAI](https://www.nuget.org/packages/OpenAI) - AI report generation
- [Docnet.Core](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Docnet.Core) - PDF text extraction
- [PdfSharpCore](https://www.nuget.org/packages/PdfSharpCore) - PDF merging and manipulation

## License

Internal use only - Rocscience

---

*Built for the Rocscience Hackathon*

projects.title: Report Generator - Edwin Yang & Danial Khan
projects.description:
We're excited to share what we accomplished during today’s hackathon! 
We built a complete AI-Powered Report Generation feature that enables users to generate, edit, and export professional technical reports directly within RSInsight.

What We Built
Report Generator Agent (AI Core) – Danial
PR: https://github.com/Rocscience/rsgpt-ai-core/pull/39
• New agent powered by Claude to generate professional, geotechnical-aware markdown reports
• Integrated as a callable tool within the orchestration agent
• Streams reports as separate SSE events (report.generated) to preserve context budget
• Supports analysis of uploaded documents via Claude Files API

Backend Support (BE) – Danial
PR: https://github.com/Rocscience/rsgpt-be/pull/59
• Proxying of report.generated events from AI Core to the frontend
• Database schema prepared for future report persistence

Frontend Report Canvas (FE) – Edwin
PR: https://github.com/Rocscience/rsgpt-fe/pull/81
• File upload to Claude Files API (up to 100MB)
• TipTap markdown editor with bidirectional parsing + WYSIWYG editing
• Collapsible Report Canvas with preview snippet
• Edit mode with full rich-text controls
• View mode with formatted markdown
• Export as text-based PDF or Markdown
• Inline streaming: reports appear inline and persist in the conversation

Technical Highlights
• TipTap + MarkedJS for markdown parsing and serialization
• SSE architecture keeps report streaming separate from primary AI responses
• Context window optimization: report output doesn’t consume token budget
• Proper text-based PDF export with pagination

![](/images/danial-edwin-h2-1.png)

Demo Flow
User requests a report and optionally uploads files

AI invokes the Report Generator

Report appears inline as a collapsible canvas

User can expand, edit, and export

Conversation continues below the report

For the demo I performed analysis in RS2, then uploaded a template PDF, and asked it to merge the results into a similar type of PDF.

Note, the Claude Files API is able to visually understand the PDF as explained in the video, https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/pdf-support.

Here are two Loom videos, please watch them sequentially, I had a limit for my free loom plan:


[Cursor - report-canvas.tsx — rsinsight (Workspace) - 10 December 2025](https://www.loom.com/share/530a2a569db9413982dbb0502eaecdca)


[Generating and Exporting Professional Reports: A Step-by-Step Guide](https://www.loom.com/share/407c082276ac478b97a5d228f7d903b5)



Limitations:

1. Claude Files API only accepts PDFs with 100 pages or less

2. Currently we do not put images into the actual generated PDF, but the report agent does understand image input

-> This can be added in the future by uploading to an S3 bucket and referencing those files before we convert the file to a PDF.

3. Currently the PDF conversation happens on the client side, it would be better if we could do this on the server side.

4. Currently this would be difficult to set up on someones machine, but I can temporarily make this available on the staging server of RSInsight for you to test.
projects.judgesNotes:
- This is an interesting approach to this problem that I hadn't really considered - very innovative
- I like how it is able to actually run or look at the file results rather than just a text file of results, could lead to interesting options
- Markdown preview and editing in place look good

Things to improve:
- obviously, the pdf is not really fully functional or polished
- the user doesn't really have a lot of control on things - I think for real reports, users would need more control of formatting and layout
- the performance could be a potential problem for a real product

projects.judgesNotes:
UI:
I like the UI - showing the defect statistics with step by step diagnosis, fix attempt, results, and the annotated geometry in the main view let's you know what it's trying very clearly. 

However, the system shows the ai repair suggestions and then completely ignores it, opting for it's own rule based system of repairing all, then only non-manifold, then only holes, etc. This was misleading to me as I thought it would follow the ai's suggestion.

functionality:
It does all of the basic things available in our repair tool, going further than just one click, it tries running the repair tools one at a time; first holes, then non manifold, etc. If the model can be fixed using the tools available in this dialog, then this system could save the user time of tediously repeating basic repair steps. 

I think this is a very reasonable thing to try and accomplish in a day. However, I would have rewarded more points for attempting to use AI in a more ambitious way, perhaps giving it images and guidelines for when to recommend to try and shrink wrap, or merge two entities, etc. 

Overall I think this is a good rule based system to help automate basic repairs with a strong UI, but suffers from a lack of ambition to use the machine learning flavor of ai to resolve larger issues.

projects.judgesNotes: Holy cow! Building a whole new geometry editor is crazy for a day. Good use of 3rd party libraries like geometry3Sharp to do geometry operations and HelixToolkit for visualization. I like the idea of creating a separate geometry editor, it makes it easier to find the relevant operations that can be performed. The use of AI to suggest which tools to use is great. I noticed that it did seem to recommend that I use all of them every time, perhaps if we gave it some more example cases for what to do if it thinks it's dealing with a tunnel vs slope, then it may be more useful. You could also try and give it images of the model.

projects.judgesNotes:
Nice job! I see you built your custom tool calling system. Ivan and Grace did something similar but used MCP with scripting. Using MCP had become more standard nowadays, and it allows you to use other people's agent systems like Cursor so that you don't have to worry about preserving message history, switching between ai models, etc, but I like that you guys implemented your own, it's cool to see and I will add points for creativity :D.

I was able to approve the ai's plans, reject and give feedback, very nice!

I tried at some point to use the repair_all_bad_features, but it removed most of my geometry. Giving the ai some way to detect that geometry wasn't removed, or maybe to allow the user to undo would be good. 

I liked that you guys tried to expose various tools other than the generic repair tool. I noticed that certain more granular options like the alpha and offset for shrink wrap weren't exposed, and I wasn't able to switch between the old geometry and the new one. 

The ui is nice, and makes it clear what the model's response was, what the plan is, and what to reply.
